page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.medium is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz, configured with 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs, resulting in 1.0 thread per core. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.e3.medium delivers modest compute and memory performance. In stress-ng testing, the single-core CPU performance scored 1102.08, while the multi-core performance reached 2162.17. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 156.12 GB/sec, which drops to 17.2 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. PassMark testing aligns with these results, yielding a CPU score of 2616.1 and a database operations score of 554.18, both falling in the bottom tier of tested systems.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.e3.medium is its low computational throughput and memory bandwidth relative to its generous 16.0 GB memory capacity. While the dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without virtualization steal-time, the underlying Intel Xeon 8269CY hardware delivers lower performance per resource compared to newer generations. This profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy but compute-light workloads. It is suitable for lightweight database operations, caching layers like Redis, and basic web serving.
